# Chart data

`pie-chart`, `bar-chart`, and a single-series `line-chart` accept the same dataset shapes.

## Accepted shapes

```typescript
// Objects are clearest when labels matter.
[
  { label: "GET", value: 450 },
  { label: "POST", value: 230 },
]

// Tuples
[["GET", 450], ["POST", 230]]

// Numbers, with labels generated by the renderer
[450, 230]

// Record keys become labels.
{ GET: 450, POST: 230 }
```

Generated labels are `Slice 1`, `Slice 2` for pie charts, `Bar 1`, `Bar 2` for bar charts, and `Point 1`, `Point 2` for line charts.

The renderer removes null entries, malformed entries, and non-finite values. Pie charts also remove zero and negative values. Bar and line charts retain finite negative and zero values.

## Static data

Store a complex static dataset in an attribute and bind `params.data` to it:

```typescript
node("requests")
  .attributes({
    requestData: [
      { label: "Mon", value: 4200 },
      { label: "Tue", value: 3800 },
    ],
  })
  .render({
    style: "bar-chart",
    params: {
      data: from.attribute("requestData"),
    },
  })
```

Complex datasets must use a supported binding rather than a direct object or array in `params`. `from.value(...)` is also valid where the style supports literal bindings, but attributes make static graph data easier to inspect.

## Live data

Define the complete dataset as one channel value, then bind `data` to that channel:

```typescript
node("requests")
  .channels([
    channel("requestData").default([
      { label: "Mon", value: 0 },
      { label: "Tue", value: 0 },
    ]),
  ])
  .render({
    style: "bar-chart",
    params: {
      data: from.channel("requestData"),
    },
  })
```

Publish a replacement array or record whenever the chart changes.

## Multiple line series

A multi-series line chart uses `datasets` instead of `data`:

```typescript
[
  {
    label: "p50",
    data: [
      { label: "Mon", value: 18 },
      { label: "Tue", value: 21 },
    ],
  },
  {
    label: "p99",
    data: [
      { label: "Mon", value: 92 },
      { label: "Tue", value: 118 },
    ],
  },
]
```

Each series accepts any single-series shape above. The renderer removes invalid and empty series.
